mainTopic: רבינא resolves the contradiction about trusting גוים with animals by splitting between לכתחילה and דיעבד. The גמרא tries to prove this split from the case of a woman imprisoned by גוים, but rejects the proof.
overview: Earlier, the גמרא raised a contradiction. Our משנה suspects גוים of bestiality, yet a ברייתא allows an animal bought from a גוי to be brought as a קרבן. רבינא answers that the משנה is about לכתחילה and the ברייתא is about דיעבד. The גמרא tries to prove this split from a woman imprisoned by גוים. The proof fails, because there the captor holds back only out of fear of losing his ransom money. רבי פדת gives a second answer: the משנה follows רבי אליעזר and the ברייתא follows רבנן. His source is their dispute over buying a פרה אדומה from a גוי. The גמרא tests this proof against other explanations of רבי אליעזר's view. One is that the גוי may have put a load on the cow. Another is the word 'וְיִקְחוּ' in the פסוק, as שֵׁילָא taught. Both are pushed away. The עמוד ends as the גמרא starts one more attempt to limit where the רבנן disagree, and this continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: רבינא: one source is before the fact, the other after
steps.stepSummary: רבינא resolves the contradiction between the משנה and the ברייתא. The משנה is about לכתחילה and the ברייתא is about דיעבד.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: There is no contradiction. The משנה tells us what to do beforehand, and the ברייתא tells us what happens after the fact.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא gives a new answer to the contradiction raised earlier. One may not leave an animal with a גוי to begin with, but if it already happened, the animal is still fit for a קרבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The concern that a גוי committed bestiality is strong enough to make us avoid the situation. It is not strong enough to disqualify an animal once the situation has already happened. So both sources are true, each in its own stage.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; there is no contradiction
Beforehand; the ideal way to act from the start
After the fact; once something has already happened

steps.whyThisMatters: The split between לכתחילה and דיעבד is one of the most common tools in all of הלכה. This step shows it applied to the question of how far we trust a גוי.

phrases.english: Ravina said: It is not difficult —
this one is ab initio, that one is after the fact.
phrases.notes: The first 'this' is our משנה (don't leave animals alone with them). The second is the ברייתא allowing a bought animal as a קרבן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers another answer to the contradiction raised before this section.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases by stage: לכתחילה versus דיעבד
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה and the ברייתא seem to disagree on whether a גוי is suspected of bestiality.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both agree on the suspicion. It forbids the situation לכתחילה but does not disqualify the animal דיעבד.

steps.title: Where do we see such a distinction?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for a source showing that, in matters of suspecting גוים, we split between לכתחילה and דיעבד.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how do you know that there is a difference here between beforehand and after the fact?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks רבינא for a source for his split. This is a setup line; the next step will offer a possible source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying 'it's only לכתחילה' could look like an easy way out of any contradiction. So the גמרא wants to see that the same split already exists elsewhere for this same suspicion.

keyTerms.meaning: And from where do you say this?
It is different; there is a difference

phrases.english: And from where do you say
that there is a difference between ab initio and after the fact?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for a source for רבינא's distinction.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that the suspicion of גוים is treated differently לכתחילה and דיעבד.

steps.title: Proof from the woman imprisoned by gentiles
steps.stepSummary: Our משנה forbids a woman from being alone with גוים. The משנה in כתובות permits a woman imprisoned by גוים over money to her husband. This seems to show the split.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in a משנה: A woman may not be alone with גוים, because they are suspected of forbidden relations. Yet another משנה teaches: A woman imprisoned by גוים over money is permitted to her husband; over a capital crime, she is forbidden. Doesn't this show that we split between beforehand and after the fact?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets two sources side by side about a woman and גוים. It suggests that the gap between them proves רבינא's split.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Forbidding a woman to be alone with them is a rule about לכתחילה. Allowing a woman who was already imprisoned to stay with her husband is a ruling about דיעבד. If the suspicion forbids the first but not the second, that is exactly the split רבינא used.

keyTerms.meaning: She may not be alone (יחוד) with them
Forbidden sexual relations
And contrast them; a contradiction from another source
Was imprisoned
Over a capital matter (her life is at stake)
Rather, isn't it so? Learn from this

phrases.english: As we learned in a mishna:
A woman may not seclude herself with them,
because they are suspected of forbidden relations.
And contrast it with another source:
A woman who was imprisoned by gentiles,
over money matters — she is permitted to her husband;
over a capital matter — she is forbidden to her husband!
Rather, isn't it so? Learn from this
that we distinguish between ab initio and after the fact?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the request for a source by offering a parallel contradiction.
steps.raayaObject: רבינא's split between לכתחילה and דיעבד regarding the suspicion of גוים.
steps.raayaSupportSource: Our משנה forbidding יחוד with גוים, compared with the משנה in כתובות permitting a woman imprisoned over money.

steps.title: Rejection: the captor fears losing his money
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. Even דיעבד we might not trust the גוי. The woman held over money is permitted only because the captor fears losing his ransom.
steps.simpleTranslation: How does that prove it? Maybe even after the fact she would not be permitted. Here the reason is different: the captor is afraid of losing his money.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the proof. It gives a different reason why the woman in כתובות is permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof assumed that the only difference between the two cases is the stage, before or after. The גמרא points to a different factor: a captor holding her for money has a strong reason to hold back, since he could lose the payment. So the כתובות case says nothing about trusting גוים דיעבד in general.

keyTerms.meaning: From where? How does that prove it?
Perhaps
Actually; really
The loss of his money

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying that רבינא's answer is wrong. It only rejects this one proof for his split; his answer itself still stands.

phrases.english: From where is that proven?
Perhaps I can actually say to you:
even after the fact, she is also not permitted,
and here, this is the reason:
that he is afraid of losing his money.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from כתובות offered in step 3.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from כתובות, not רבינא's answer itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The כתובות case has its own special reason, the captor's fear of losing money. So it is not about לכתחילה versus דיעבד.

steps.title: The end of that משנה confirms the money reason
steps.stepSummary: The end of the משנה in כתובות forbids a woman held over a capital crime. This shows that the money factor is what made the difference.
steps.simpleTranslation: Know that this is so, because the end of that משנה teaches: if she was held over a capital matter, she is forbidden to her husband. Nothing more needs to be said.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא supports its rejection with the end of that same משנה. It closes the discussion: the case is clear.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both cases in the משנה are after the fact, yet one is permitted and one is forbidden. The only difference is whether money is at stake. So the reason must be the captor's fear of losing money, not a general split between לכתחילה and דיעבד.

keyTerms.meaning: Know that this is so; a support for what was just said
The last clause of a משנה or ברייתא
And nothing more; the matter is settled

steps.whatToRemember: רבינא splits the cases into לכתחילה and דיעבד. The proof from the imprisoned woman fails, because there the captor holds back only out of fear of losing his money. This is clear from the סיפא, where no money is at stake and she is forbidden.

phrases.english: Know that this is so, for the latter clause teaches:
over a capital matter, she is forbidden to her husband,
and nothing more needs to be said.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the rejection in step 4 with the end of the כתובות משנה.
steps.raayaObject: The rejection's claim that the woman is permitted only because the captor fears losing money.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The סיפא of the משנה in כתובות: a woman held over a capital matter is forbidden.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The כתובות case cannot prove a general split between לכתחילה and דיעבד. Its leniency rests on the captor's financial reason to hold back.

steps.title: רבי פדת: The Two Sources Follow Different תנאים
steps.stepSummary: רבי פדת offers a second resolution. The משנה follows רבי אליעזר, and the ברייתא follows רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי פדת said: It is not a contradiction. This one follows רבי אליעזר, and that one follows רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי פדת gives a new way to answer the contradiction between our משנה and the ברייתא. He says they simply follow two different opinions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבינא kept both sources in agreement by splitting לכתחילה from דיעבד. רבי פדת takes a different path. He says there is a real dispute: our משנה, which suspects a גוי of רביעה, follows רבי אליעזר, and the ברייתא, which allows an animal bought from a גוי as a קרבן, follows רבנן.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; there is no contradiction
This one... that one... (matching each source to a different case or opinion)

phrases.english: Rabbi Pedat said:
It is not difficult —
this is Rabbi Eliezer, that is the Rabbis.
phrases.notes: "This" is our משנה, which suspects רביעה. "That" is the ברייתא, which allows the animal as a קרבן.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי פְּדָת אָמַר: לָא קַשְׁיָא — הָא רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר, הָא רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers an alternative to רבינא's answer from Step 1, after the side discussion in Steps 2-5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing each source to a different תנא (תנאי היא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה and ברייתא contradict each other about suspecting a גוי of רביעה.
steps.terutzMaskana: They do disagree, but each follows a different side of a dispute between תנאים.

steps.title: Proof from the Dispute About Buying a פרה אדומה
steps.stepSummary: רבי פדת brings the משנה about פרה אדומה. רבי אליעזר forbids buying it from a גוי, and חכמים allow it. He suggests that the dispute is about suspecting רביעה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned about the פרה אדומה: רבי אליעזר says it may not be bought from גוים, and the חכמים permit it. Isn't their dispute about this: רבי אליעזר holds we worry about רביעה, and רבנן hold we do not?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי פדת shows where רבי אליעזר and רבנן disagree. He reads their dispute about buying a פרה אדומה from a גוי as a dispute about whether we suspect רביעה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An animal that was used for רביעה is not fit for the מזבח, and it is not fit as a פרה אדומה either. So if רבי אליעזר refuses to buy a פרה אדומה from a גוי, the reason could be the worry about רביעה. רבנן, who permit buying it, would then have no such worry.

keyTerms.meaning: The red heifer (פרה אדומה), whose ashes are used for purification
Bestiality; an animal used this way is unfit for holy use
We are concerned; we suspect
Is it not that...? (introduces a suggested reading)
They disagree

phrases.english: As we learned regarding the red heifer:
Rabbi Eliezer says:
it may not be bought from gentiles,
and the Sages permit it.
Is it not that they disagree about this:
that Rabbi Eliezer holds:
we are concerned about bestiality,
and the Rabbis hold:
we are not concerned about bestiality?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for רבי פדת's claim that רבי אליעזר and רבנן disagree about suspecting רביעה.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי אליעזר suspects a גוי of רביעה and רבנן do not.
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה in פרה 2:1: the dispute about buying a פרה אדומה from גוים.

steps.title: Maybe the Worry Is Work, Not רביעה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. Maybe everyone agrees there is no worry of רביעה, and רבי אליעזר's worry is that the גוי placed a load on the cow. Even a bundle of sacks disqualifies a פרה אדומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do you know this? Perhaps everyone agrees we are not concerned about רביעה. רבי אליעזר's reason here follows רב יהודה in the name of רב: if someone placed a bundle of sacks on it, he disqualified it. But an עגלה ערופה is not disqualified until it pulls a load. So one holds we are concerned about work, and the other holds we are not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רבי פדת's proof. It offers a different reason for רבי אליעזר's view that has nothing to do with רביעה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A פרה אדומה becomes unfit even from a light load, like a bundle of sacks placed on it. So רבי אליעזר may only be worried that the גוי put something on the cow, while רבנן are not worried about that. If so, the dispute is about work, and it tells us nothing about רביעה.

keyTerms.meaning: From where (do you know)? Introduces a challenge to a proof
Perhaps
Everyone agrees
A bundle of sacks
The calf whose neck is broken for an unsolved murder

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two animals. The פרה אדומה is disqualified even by a load just lying on it. The עגלה ערופה is disqualified only if it actually pulls something.

phrases.english: From where do you know this?
Perhaps everyone agrees
that we are not concerned about bestiality,
and here this is Rabbi Eliezer's reason —
in line with what Rav Yehuda said in the name of Rav,
as Rav Yehuda said in the name of Rav:
if he placed upon it a bundle of sacks —
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the word in round brackets; the corrected wording, in square brackets, is "on it," meaning the פרה אדומה.

phrases.english: he disqualified it,
but with the calf — not until it pulls with it.
phrases.notes: "The calf" is the עגלה ערופה. It becomes unfit only once it actually drags a load.

phrases.english: One Sage holds we are concerned,
phrases.notes: This is רבי אליעזר. He worries the גוי put a load on the cow.

phrases.english: and the other Sage holds we are not concerned!

steps.triggerLanguage: מִמַּאי? דִּלְמָא דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא חָיְישִׁינַן לִרְבִיעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבי פדת's reading of the פרה אדומה dispute from Step 7.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof is rejected. רבי פדת's answer may still be true, but this source does not show it.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי אליעזר's ruling can be explained by a worry about the cow carrying a load, which applies only to פרה אדומה, so the ruling need not be about רביעה.

steps.title: A גוי Would Not Ruin a Big Sale for a Small Convenience
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the work explanation. A גוי would not lose the large profit from selling a פרה אדומה just for the small convenience of putting sacks on it.
steps.simpleTranslation: That cannot enter your mind. For a small convenience, he would not lose a lot of money.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי פדת. It says the work explanation does not make sense, so רבי אליעזר's worry must really be רביעה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A פרה אדומה sells for a very high price. A גוי knows this and would not risk ruining it just to save a little effort by resting sacks on it. So the worry of a load is too unlikely, and רבי פדת's reading about רביעה stands again.

keyTerms.meaning: It cannot enter your mind; that idea is impossible
A small convenience
He will not lose a lot

phrases.english: That cannot enter your mind,
because for a small convenience
he would not lose a lot.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ, מִשּׁוּם נִיחָא פּוּרְתָּא לָא מַפְסֵיד טוּבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the alternative explanation from Step 8 and restores רבי פדת's proof.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the suggestion that רבי אליעזר's worry is about the cow carrying a load.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A גוי would not risk a large profit for a small convenience, so the worry about a load is not realistic.

steps.title: The Same Logic Should Apply to רביעה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges back: by the same reasoning, a גוי would not lose a big sale for the small pleasure of רביעה either.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then let us also say: for a small pleasure, he would not lose a lot of money.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the argument from the last step against רבי פדת's reading. If money stops the גוי from putting sacks on the cow, it should stop him from רביעה too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The argument in Step 9 was that a big profit keeps the גוי careful. That same argument seems to remove the worry of רביעה as well. If it does, רבי אליעזר's ruling is left without any explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: So too, let us say (applying the same logic)
Pleasure, enjoyment

phrases.english: So too, let us say:
because of a small pleasure
he would not lose a lot!

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי נָמֵי לֵימָא: מִשּׁוּם הֲנָאָה פּוּרְתָּא לָא מַפְסֵיד טוּבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the reasoning of Step 9 against the רביעה explanation itself.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי אליעזר suspects רביעה when buying a פרה אדומה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the fear of losing money stops a small convenience, it should also stop a small pleasure. Then there would be no worry of רביעה either.

steps.title: With רביעה, His Desire Overpowers Him
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רביעה is different, because desire overpowers a person even against his own financial interest.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why money logic works for a load but not for רביעה. Desire can make a person act against his own interest.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Putting sacks on a cow is a calm choice, so a person weighs the cost and avoids it. רביעה comes from strong desire, which can push aside careful thinking about money. So רבי אליעזר may still worry about רביעה, and רבי פדת's answer stands.

keyTerms.meaning: There (in the other case)
His (evil) inclination overpowers him

steps.whatToRemember: רבי פדת says the משנה follows רבי אליעזר, who suspects רביעה, and the ברייתא follows רבנן, who do not. The worry is about רביעה, not about a load, because a person weighs money carefully, but desire can override that.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a clear principle: a financial reason can stop a person from a small convenience, but it does not reliably stop him from acting on strong desire.

phrases.english: There, his inclination overpowers him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 10 by separating desire from calm convenience.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The money reason should rule out רביעה just as it rules out placing a load.
steps.terutzMaskana: Desire overpowers a person's sense of financial interest, so the worry about רביעה remains.

steps.title: Maybe רבי אליעזר learns his rule from the word 'take'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא offers a new way to push away the proof. Maybe nobody worries about רביעה, and רבי אליעזר's reason is the פסוק 'וְיִקְחוּ אֵלֶיךָ' as שֵׁילָא taught: only בני ישראל take the פרה, not גוים.
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe everyone agrees there is no worry about רביעה. Here רבי אליעזר's reason is what שֵׁילָא taught: the פסוק says 'Speak to the children of Israel, and they shall take to you.' This means Jews take the פרה, and גוים do not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives another reason why רבי פדת's proof might not work. Maybe רבי אליעזר's rule has nothing to do with רביעה and comes from a פסוק instead.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי פדת wanted to show that רבי אליעזר suspects רביעה. Now the גמרא says the rule could come straight from the word 'וְיִקְחוּ', which says the פרה must come from בני ישראל. If so, the dispute tells us nothing about רביעה, and the proof is gone.

keyTerms.meaning: And perhaps; this opens a different possibility that weakens a proof
Everyone; both sides of the dispute
An early teacher who taught a ברייתא explaining רבי אליעזר's reason
And they shall take; the word in the פסוק about the פרה אדומה

steps.confusionAlert: This is a fresh explanation of רבי אליעזר, not a return to the 'load on the cow' idea from step 8. Here the reason is a פסוק, not any worry about what the גוי did.

phrases.english: And perhaps everyone agrees
that we are not concerned about bestiality,
and here, this is Rabbi Eliezer's reason:
as Sheila taught, for Sheila taught:
What is Rabbi Eliezer's reason?
"Speak to the children of Israel, and they shall take to you"
the children of Israel shall take it,
but the gentiles shall not take it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְדִלְמָא דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא חָיְישִׁינַן לִרְבִיעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the 'load' explanation failed (steps 9–11), the גמרא offers a different way to explain רבי אליעזר without רביעה.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רבי פדת's proof that the dispute is about suspecting רביעה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי אליעזר's rule may come from a פסוק ('וְיִקְחוּ') and not from any suspicion

steps.title: The word 'take' cannot explain all offerings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects שֵׁילָא's explanation. The end of the same teaching says רבי אליעזר disqualifies animals from a גוי for all קרבנות, but the word קיחה is written only by the פרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do not think that. The end of that teaching says: 'And likewise רבי אליעזר disqualified in all the offerings.' If his reason were like שֵׁילָא's, that works for the פרה, since 'taking' is written there. But is 'taking' written about all the other offerings?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the explanation from the word 'take', which brings back the idea that רבי אליעזר worries about רביעה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר's rule reaches every קרבן, not just the פרה. The word 'וְיִקְחוּ' appears only by the פרה, so it cannot be the source for all קרבנות. That means his reason must be something wider, like suspecting רביעה, and רבי פדת's proof is back in play.

keyTerms.meaning: Do not think so; that idea cannot be right
The end part of a teaching
Disqualifies
Granted; this works well for one case, then the גמרא asks about another
Taking; the word used in the פסוק about the פרה

steps.whyThisMatters: Because רבי אליעזר's rule covers every קרבן, any explanation of it has to work for every קרבן. A word written about only one קרבן cannot explain them all.

phrases.english: It should not enter your mind,
for the latter clause teaches:
And likewise Rabbi Eliezer would disqualify
in all of the offerings.
And if it enters your mind that it is as Sheila taught,
granted, the heifer:
"taking" is written about it,
but all the other offerings,
is "taking" written about them?

steps.title: Maybe the רבנן argue with רבי אליעזר only in some cases
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins a new suggestion: maybe the רבנן disagree with רבי אליעזר only in a limited area. The sentence continues on the next עמוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: But perhaps the רבנן disagree with רבי אליעזר only...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is starting a new way to push away the proof. This is only the opening words, and the rest of the sentence comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'עַד כָּאן לָא פְּלִיגִי' means 'they argue only in this case'. The גמרא is about to limit where the רבנן actually disagree with רבי אליעזר. That could change what the dispute proves about רביעה.

keyTerms.meaning: They only argue up to this point; their dispute is limited to a certain case
